In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PGE2, IL-23 and/or IL-1β synergize to induce a Th17 response in human cells and that PGE2 preferentially induces IL-17A over IL-17F, which may be important for mucosal health and inflammation.
PGE2 is a potent inducer of IL-17A production by T cells and this effect is synergistically potentiated by IL-23 and/or IL-1β.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

PGE2, IL-23 and PGE2 plus IL-23 plus L1β differentially modulate IL-17A and IL-17F gene expression by regulating chromatin structure and histone modifications at the IL17A locus and the IL17F locus in Th17 memory cells.
PGE2 enhances the IL-17A response in Th17 cells, and this is likely due to a distinct chromatin configuration at the IL17A locus.
PGE2 is a potent enhancer of the IL17A locus, but not the IL17F locus, which may have important implications for the development of IL-17 mediated inflammatory disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that

IL17A and its gene locus are poised for expression in Th17 cells and that PGE2 enhances Th17 cell IL-17A production by promoting a switch from an epigenetic landscape favoring IL-17F transcription to one that favors IL-17A transcription.
